title: Module Review Quiz: Modern C++ Features & Type Traits

slides.title: Modern C++ Features & Type Traits Overview
slides.prompt: This Module Quiz covers modern C++ features (C++11 to C++20) including auto type deduction, constexpr, static_assert, std::optional, std::variant, compile-time type traits (<type_traits>), and C++20 Concepts & Constraints (CPP_273 to CPP_280).

slides.title: Auto Type Deduction (CPP_273)
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword introduced in C++11 for automatic type deduction of variables.

slides.title: decltype Specifier (CPP_273)
slides.prompt: What is the primary usage of 'decltype' in modern C++?
options: To inspect and yield the declared type of an expression at compile-time
To convert floating-point numbers to integers dynamically
To declare a new variable on heap memory
To clear exception flags from input streams
slides.correctAnswer: To inspect and yield the declared type of an expression at compile-time

slides.title: Compile-time Constant (CPP_274)
slides.prompt: Fill in the specifier keyword used to evaluate functions or constants at compile-time.

slides.title: static_assert Validation (CPP_275)
slides.prompt: When does 'static_assert(condition, message)' perform its evaluation check?
options: At runtime when function is invoked

slides.title: std::optional Value Presence (CPP_276)
slides.prompt: Fill in the member function name used to check if a std::optional contains a value.

slides.title: std::variant Storage (CPP_277)
options: A type-safe, type-discriminated union holding one value from a set of types
A dynamic array that can hold multiple different types at once
A pointer that points to variable memory locations
An enum class wrapper for integer values
slides.correctAnswer: A type-safe, type-discriminated union holding one value from a set of types

slides.title: Accessing std::variant (CPP_277)
slides.prompt: Fill in the template helper function name used to retrieve a specific type value from std::variant.
slides.codeSnippet:
std::variant<int, string> v = 42;
int val = std::___<int>(v);

slides.title: std::any Container (CPP_277)
slides.prompt: Which function is used to safely cast and extract a value stored inside a 'std::any' instance?

slides.title: Type Traits Header (CPP_278)
slides.prompt: Fill in the header file name required to inspect and modify types at compile-time.

slides.title: Type Trait Suffix _v (CPP_278)
slides.prompt: In C++17 type traits, what does 'std::is_same_v<T, U>' represent?
options: A helper variable template equal to 'std::is_same<T, U>::value'
A void pointer to the runtime type information
A virtual class method evaluating dynamic types
A vector storing type comparison results
slides.correctAnswer: A helper variable template equal to 'std::is_same<T, U>::value'

slides.title: Compile-time If (CPP_278)
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword combination introduced in C++17 for compile-time branch selection.

slides.title: C++20 Concepts Purpose (CPP_279)
slides.prompt: What is the primary benefit of C++20 Concepts in template programming?
options: They enforce compile-time constraints on template arguments, producing clear error messages
They allow templates to execute faster during runtime
They convert template code into non-template binary functions
They automatically manage dynamic memory deallocation
slides.correctAnswer: They enforce compile-time constraints on template arguments, producing clear error messages

slides.title: C++20 Requires Clause (CPP_280)
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used in C++20 to specify constraints on template parameters.

slides.title: Defining a Concept (CPP_280)
slides.prompt: Which syntax correctly defines a custom C++20 Concept named 'Integral'?
options: template <typename T> struct concept Integral = std::is_integral_v<T>;
